document.title: Colorado Academic Standards: Reading, Writing and Communicating

0181C9A095D7411E919520AC12C789A5.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

01D53E0E417C4C5D927A0232446B9F47.description: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.

06595F429BDF41AEB57CD923083EBF51.description: Write informative/explanatory texts using text structures appropriate for the purpose and developed through facts, definitions, concrete details, precise language, and domain-specific vocabulary.

0676907BA841480E9AE19CF50FA0616B.description: Apply strategies to comprehend and interpret informational texts.

07ED76B625F142A489564B62732AF13E.description: Create a plan to effectively present information both informally and formally.

0EED124C38B941E89061DCA1F005D9D9.description: Consult reference materials (for example: dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

10D1FFC7C563475C875D257FEF4E7D3A.description: Pose thoughtful questions after actively listening to others.

19C8AC11B5A2466E99CB9906CD838B7D.description: Read familiar texts orally with fluency, accuracy, and prosody (expression).

1C686BC91FB34F11907742AF3D22065C.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

1CEA02D4CA314731ADBC52D546F3CC99.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

200F7C9D77C34013A75E4E3AF88E610C.description: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.

22492DA041814F6A9420377ED0B34A66.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (for example: to, too, two; there, their)

258AA09080BB4E4A90B00CA2ED140015.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

25B24AC0691A4EC4BB3495223BD92FB8.description: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (for example: headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

263000AF66144C89849EA878F5743D58.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (for example: "Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text").

2708B10C486F4DEA82A4922C132775FC.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

2749AB5BFE2244EBAA56491291C8D572.description: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

2BDC54DE184C41EAB8A7A9C6821F0BF5.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (for example: telegraph, photograph, autograph).

2E6F583E6CB54A21AC9FE3CBFB253978.description: Read and understand words with common prefixes (for example: un-, re-, dis-) and derivational suffixes ( for example: -ful, -ly, -ness)

2F5D22A076764958A172247B76E915B5.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

35020A19C8414B0491A80B5C3CD58712.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (for example: presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (for example: small-group discussion).

3938D557007E427E92B3C0BDDF2C2B30.description: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.

3A5F7EA4EB524E76B820BFF99334D712.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

3A754742C1304231BB7C4300844064A7.description: Use Range of Reading and Complexity of Text to:

3AA05CB46D6748668AD99058DC069DA4.description: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.

3B2C8BA93DD64F05B3AB4558E99A250C.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (for example: presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (for example: small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

3FB4E21B585B45AE9B29327C70ED7AC4.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

41A2A5DEB3954852835DC794ED92D17A.description: Use modal auxiliaries (for example: can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

41B3FC25CB7B4000B9C270BFA7FB79F4.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

465992E2771746C584F775F0D370D661.description: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.

46EEAB310F034779AE80D8B9FB529D20.description: Use Key Ideas and Details to:

495E7D0C47BE4635A4083D2CDDF432E2.description: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:

4B08E8447AD1463F9E9EF0573BC55212.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (for example, roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

4B17E3E1F63A44508F67320944AFF00D.description: Use context (for example: definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

4C63F23A302F4C0EA440EEC5EE652E85.description: Read multisyllabic words with and without inflectional and derivational suffixes

50A01D4F4059473BBC556AA3900E33B2.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

5109F77880624549B1326D1164326639.description: Write engaging, real or imagined narratives using descriptive details and dialogue to convey a sequence of related events.

56C629078E8B495FAAF3EEA1293CDC2D.description: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.

57A848B69E1F4D0095B4D4B5A8D6B79B.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.

5A459B33DE5440BC9E795F42DB1E305F.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

5BB1368D654B4A1B9F7D24588C446B35.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

5D5242F0F1E146FCABC81A6365694B7A.description: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.

5D7488396729498FBD0B2AF16C2BE69D.description: Identify a text structure appropriate to purpose (sequence, chronology, description, explanation, and comparison-and-contrast).

5E95E203314640489BFD63D84DA4B5A0.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

627E8D8945A64E0EBB29BD89384DFCC2.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

63D84DC866B94BB991C6D91306F25B1C.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

64D1D5F1E7DF4671B38E33B29AD4878F.description: Use Range of Reading and Complexity of Text to:

6DD77A849EF34067854D6BC95A6BDEFB.description: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).

6E25906530AE48E29C36A0478FEBE799.description: Describe the development of plot (such as the origin of the central conflict, the action of the plot, and how the conflict is resolved).

6E7F85C20B75402B889F8B32CD57C1D5.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

6F11538356E6485BB4A25A31970EDA6A.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.

71A12161F5FB46E4834672E9A1732E53.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (for example: a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

737C420CA84A46C38DF1932F1516EB01.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (for example: "Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text [for example: a character's thoughts, words, or actions].").

741E76AAAD0244B6B72887D24BB014B0.description: Apply strategies to comprehend and interpret literary texts.

76888D5B72B04C80A51BED3869EA3772.description: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (for example: another, for example, also, because).

7B6B9090257E49F28ADF3F4D8B37300C.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

7B86AF74F940426B82622BE3AD125345.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

8025426A0A3449888AA5EA2087420A5A.description: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 4–5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

826B7A5F76BF43E4BB07230FCA30B4C1.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology (for example: Herculean).

8547F55E5A234F89AE5AEEC11347DB24.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts supporting a point of view with reasons and information.

85BA86ACFC274532825E8FBC78DCED5E.description: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (for example: in charts, graphs, diagrams, time lines, animations, or interactive elements on Web pages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.

86B7D035E1974BD0AD33612800EBDC77.description: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (for example: for instance, in order to, in addition).

8B78329C7F39461A8A3AB53E344A91BA.description: Produce complete simple, compound, and complex sentences.

8BBD431ECF414FC986DFFDDB16774081.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

8F92499007164E4694D9CBCFD5C956E3.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (for example, as pretty as a picture) in context.

900FDC7CF14F434883F50641026BFB05.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

93E37C582E65443894A788226A73390B.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

9541340E3C53489D8DA111DE108B9816.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.

958C8D938885489BB055F6A6058BA1DD.description: Describe the overall structure (for example, chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.

9F0FC49A657D4CD0B77361A97BA81720.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

A01C9D66343A484FBB592A643906AB85.description: Identify a topic and formulate open-ended research questions for further inquiry and learning.

A12AE62F9D8F40268998D1BF98C7B434.description: Use a variety of resources to build and communicate knowledge related to open-ended research questions.

A1CEEB3EF0A54B008E69E2C6425BBFEF.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

A2633326FD9A443EA7D892E67296196F.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

A3348E460EF44BB581ED457E110C4FA1.description: Infer meaning of words using explanations offered within a text.

A6D9FB7827D24BF4846E13EA3C72703F.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

ABBF0955A4D744DF8F981AA1685C2F95.description: Present a brief report of the research findings to an audience.

AC7626D6B16C49C5B6CB1494B3C4AAF3.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

B1765B037AA74C89BCBF496886D7E372.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

B385B903F7A64823AEFE790AC6AEE70C.description: Read and understand words that change spelling to show past tense (for example: write/wrote, catch/caught, teach/taught)

B6D03B1F91B34315945B6EB9A88DDCE6.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

BB204ACF723146D5A0B70B19EBA3993A.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

BD2A48FA18D8483493A8E503C5134F22.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

C094DADB521340BF8772456AF2046B71.description: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

C1E5F4135D7C4913A919A1194577DBDC.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

C7CB9791D38E461183ECBA89E0C3169A.description: Form and use the progressive (for example: I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

CC3BF206049F438DBE8E7E5C189F58AE.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

CE88D79AC9D1479189CC6D6B4CE275DA.description: Apply knowledge of spelling patterns (orthography) and word meanings (morphology) to decode multisyllable words and determine the meaning of unknown words.

CF57E7160836415DA5A3B5CFACFE1390.description: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (for example: opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (for example: the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.

D9A99D0A487B4819A5AB631CF5BEB156.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.

DC4481E48C1F493C9EDB4751EAA23A74.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

DE20AC71FA25437ABC1025A603C95E0E.description: Use Key Ideas and Details to:

E34F63AF17E64914BA77F62B2A2749B6.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (for example: quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (for example: wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

E3A72E5A1DB546CE9481D909C2E99D3B.description: Organize relevant ideas and details to convey a central idea or prove a point.

E7DDDC48A44D4BBB891707558BE173B1.description: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.

EFDF2994D6824C6BAACDF264759CD2A6.description: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (for example: a character's thoughts, words, or actions).

F0709F458EBE41018AB623CF007361F9.description: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

F1A341B456CA4BE996CBCE3746C9F1F8.description: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.

F2FF70CAA6C04A0594E5D06DFBAB2ADC.description: Use compound subjects (for example: Tom and Pat went to the store) and compound verbs (for example: Harry thought and worried about the things he said to Jane) to create sentence fluency in writing

F3A82F00C40146C3905D321EFA52F673.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points

F419854A1C8C40499E31D24F99A58E30.description: Understand why and how writers use the conventions of Standard English grammar, usage, and mechanics to clarify their meaning.

F792560C736F48FFB500CF894FD4BA9C.description: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of poems (for example: verse, rhythm, meter) and drama (for example, casts of characters, settings, descriptions, dialogue, stage directions) when writing or speaking about a text.

F7EAF1513A7842C896FE29248050322C.description: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:

F818F33A17A84E1F8BE2AC709AAC9DA8.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

F8473F88A93B4E02892FF0CB95E86622.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

FBC9052526D8404889959E9B6F5B392E.description: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text, identifying where each version reflects specific descriptions and directions in the text.

FC97B17EB0964C46B3F0E8D1906CB037.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.

FE9AF1189D9E44F6BFC2F1E3B23280CC.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.

FF34111E6991486B829CC1CD1F38DD09.description: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.
